requirements.description: Research must focus on next-generation AI agents as autonomous systems powered by large AI language models (LLMs or large multimodal models) capable of autonomous planning, tool use, and goal-directed action based on high-level instructions.

Proposals should address key aspects of effective AI agent design including robust planning, reasoning, and search mechanisms that allow agents to approach complex tasks by breaking them down into structured subgoals.
Proposals should address effective memory and state management through a balanced integration of short-term and external long-term memory solutions for coherent long-term agent interactions.
Proposals should address integration of external tools and APIs to overcome limitations in large AI models and enhance agent performance in tasks requiring accuracy and reliability.
Potential research area: enhancing AI agent autonomy through advanced self-planning and self-optimization capabilities, enabling agents to improve their decision-making and strategic planning.
Potential research area: innovation in memory-augmented AI agents to facilitate robust long-term reasoning and lifelong learning.
Potential research area: developing advanced multi-agent frameworks specifically tailored for collaborative agents, including research on AI agent frameworks based on mixed AI architectures.
Potential research area: advancing multimodal reasoning capabilities to enable real-world applications.
All proposals are expected to incorporate mechanisms for assessing and demonstrating progress, including qualitative and quantitative KPIs, benchmarking, and progress monitoring.
Projects selected in this topic should link to the resources offered by the AI Factories, including the Data Labs.
Communicable results should be shared with the European R&D community through the AI-on-demand platform.
All proposals are expected to allocate tasks for cohesion activities with ADRA and the CSA HORIZON-CL4-2025-03-HUMAN-18: GenAI4EU central Hub.
Proposals should build on or seek collaboration with relevant projects and develop synergies with other relevant International, European, national, or regional initiatives.
When possible, proposals should build on and reuse public results from relevant previous funded actions.
Results may be validated in the Testing and Experiment Facilities (TEFs) and further deployed via the European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs).

Proposals should demonstrate relevance to Apply AI application sectors; the portfolio coverage rule prioritises at least one funded project per each of the three named sectors: healthcare, advanced manufacturing, and in-vehicle autonomous driving.
